title: Multiplying without barriers with Soroban, Suanpan (算盤) and Schyoty (счёты)
header: Multiplying without barriers with Soroban, Suanpan (算盤) and Schyoty (счёты)

text.text:
### Prerequisites

This lesson continues an earlier game in which we multiplied a number with several place values (ones, tens, hundreds, ...) by a number made up only of ones (<htcite0>). Since every step here builds on that calculation, we suggest that you practice with that earlier game before moving on, so that you can follow each step of the multiplication with ease.

text.text:
### Introduction

Our study of multiplication has been built step by step. In the previous step, we learned to multiply a number — no matter which place values it has (ones, tens, hundreds, and so on) — by a single-digit number (<htcite0>).

However, as the following texts show, there are situations in which we also need to multiply a large number by a number that has more than one digit, for example 43 × 26. To do this, we will call once more on the concepts presented during the rereading (<htcite1>) and build the new steps on top of them.

text.text:
Reflection 1: Next step

We saw that, thanks to our rereading of numbers, we can begin the multiplication with the largest place values and then keep adding the results that come from the other place values ().

From now on, every number in this text will have at least two place values (ones and tens). With that in mind, how could you use these place values to make the multiplication easier?

text.text:
### Multiplying by larger numbers

The general idea of how to multiply by larger numbers was already presented in the rereading text (<htcite0>). To make those steps clearer, we will use once again the abacuses developed in China (Zhongguo 中國), Japan (Nippon koku or Nihon koku, 日本国) and Russia: the Suanpan (算盤), the Soroban (算盤) and the Schyoty (счёты).

To multiply a number by a number greater than 9, follow the steps below. Our example will be 25 × 25:
- **Step 1 — Split the number into its place values.** For example, 25 becomes 20 + 5.
- **Step 2 — Multiply by the tens.** In our example, we multiply by 2 and obtain 25 × 2 = 50. We then shift that result one place to the left — in other words, we multiply it by 10 — which gives 500. (On the abacus, this is the same as adding a zero at the end.)
- **Step 3 — Multiply by the ones.** In our example, we multiply by 5 and obtain 25 × 5 = 125.
- **Step 4 — Add the two partial results.** We add the result of the multiplication by the tens to the result of the multiplication by the ones: 500 + 125 = 625. This is the final product.

Do not worry if this description still seems complex. In the next section you will carry out the procedure in practice, with the app guiding you through every step of the process.

### The Abacus (Multiplication)

Because homework exercises are a good way to reinforce what we learn (<htcite0>), the abacus below runs a multiplication for you and explains, step by step, every stage of the calculation performed with this tool.

#### How an exercise works

Each exercise asks you to build a single product on the abacus. To calculate 25 × 25, for instance, you will go through four phases:
- Multiply by the tens (2 in our example) and shift the result one place to the left.
- Keep that result in the box below the abacus.
- Reset the abacus and multiply by the ones (5 in our example).
- Add the stored result to reach the final product.

The instruction on the screen always tells you what to do at the current stage, and the message at the bottom of the abacus tells you whether you got it right.

#### Levels

The game has 5 levels, ordered by the number of digits of the first factor:

- **Level 1**: 1-digit numbers (1 to 9)
- **Level 2**: 2-digit numbers (10 to 19)
- **Level 3**: 3-digit numbers (100 to 199)
- **Level 4**: 4-digit numbers (1,000 to 1,999)
- **Level 5**: 5-digit numbers (10,000 to 19,999)

Use the "⭐ Next level" button to move on to the next level. On level 5, the button takes you back to level 1.

#### Multiplier

The dropdown selector next to the level badge chooses the tens of the multiplier: 10, 20, 30, ..., 90. The game then adds a random ones digit from 1 to 9, so choosing "30" can give you 30 + 7 = 37. Choose "Randomly" to draw a different tens value on every exercise.

#### Abacus modes

The buttons at the bottom let you switch among the three abacuses — Soroban, Suanpan and Schyoty — and move the decimal marker. The value on the abacus is kept, and the steps of the calculation stay the same.

#### How to play

Between the bar with the "🎲 New exercise" and "⭐ Next level" buttons and the "➡ Next step" button, you will see an instruction describing what to do at the current stage. As soon as you complete that stage correctly, a message congratulating you appears at the bottom of the abacus: "✅ Correct! Click 'Next step' to continue."

Keep following the steps until the calculation is complete; you will then see your product celebrated with "🎉🎉🎉 PERFECT! 🎉🎉🎉" and the message "Great job using the abacus!"

Press the "⭐ Next level" button while you are on level 5 and you will receive the following message: "🏅 Congratulations! You reached the last level! 🏅"

You can repeat as many exercises as you wish at the same level: simply click "🎲 New exercise" after finishing a calculation.

source.text: Costa, M., Cardoso, A. P., Lacerda, C., Lopes, A., & Gomes, C.

### Conclusion

In this text we have seen, through the Soroban (算盤), the Suanpan (算盤) and the Schyoty (счёты), that multiplying one number by another follows the same logic as multiplying by a single-digit number, no matter how many place values (ones, tens, hundreds, ...) either number has. We multiply each place value separately and then add the partial results together to obtain the final product.
